clusters.title: Inline Suggestion Latency Disrupts Flow
clusters.summary: Users report noticeable delays of 1-3 seconds before ghost text appears, especially in large files or monorepos, forcing them to pause mid-thought and wait. This breaks the cognitive flow that Copilot promises to enhance, making it feel like a hindrance rather than an accelerator on slower connections or complex codebases.
verbatims: I work in a monorepo with 200k+ lines and the ghost text just... sits there spinning. By the time the suggestion shows up I've already typed the whole line myself. It's faster to not use it.

The latency is my biggest complaint. In small toy projects it feels magical, but the second I open my actual work repo the inline suggestions lag so bad I had to disable them and just use the chat panel instead.
On my home WiFi it's borderline unusable — I get a 2-second freeze every time Copilot tries to autocomplete a function signature. My colleagues on faster connections don't believe me when I complain.

clusters.title: Suggestions Ignore Surrounding Codebase Context
clusters.summary: Copilot frequently generates code that contradicts existing abstractions, duplicates utility functions already defined elsewhere in the project, or suggests patterns inconsistent with the established architecture. Users feel they spend more time correcting contextually wrong suggestions than they save from accepting correct ones.
verbatims: It keeps suggesting I create a new fetchUser() helper when I literally have one defined in /utils/api.ts that it should know about. It's like it only reads the current file and nothing else.

We have a strict internal design system and Copilot insists on suggesting raw inline styles and Material UI components we don't use. Every suggestion in a React component is wrong by default because it has no clue about our architecture.

I asked Copilot Chat to add error handling to a function and it invented a completely different error class than what our codebase uses. It had access to the workspace and still got it wrong. Frustrating doesn't cover it.

clusters.title: Copilot Chat Confidently Invents API Methods
clusters.summary: Users consistently report that Copilot Chat generates plausible-sounding but non-existent library methods, deprecated function signatures, and fabricated SDK parameters, often without any caveat. Because the output looks authoritative and syntactically correct, junior developers especially waste significant time debugging code that was never valid to begin with.
verbatims: It told me to call stripe.subscriptions.listUpcoming() with complete confidence. That method does not exist in the Stripe SDK. I spent 45 minutes reading docs before I realized Copilot just made it up.

Copilot Chat gave me a whole working-looking implementation using a pandas method called df.group_transform() — I copy-pasted it, got AttributeError, searched for 10 minutes, and discovered the method is completely fictional. No warning, no 'I'm not sure.'
The hallucinated APIs are a real trust-breaker. I now have to verify every single method it suggests against the actual docs, which defeats half the purpose of using it in the first place.

clusters.title: Generated Tests Lack Edge Cases and Depth
clusters.summary: When using Copilot to generate unit or integration tests, users find the output covers only the happy path with trivial assertions, omitting boundary conditions, error states, and async edge cases that actually matter. Teams report that relying on Copilot-generated tests creates false confidence in coverage metrics without meaningfully validating business logic.
verbatims: I asked it to write tests for my authentication middleware and it gave me three tests that all check if a valid token returns 200. Nothing for expired tokens, malformed headers, rate limiting, any of it. I had to write all the real tests myself anyway.

The tests it generates are basically useless for anything non-trivial. It'll test that a function returns a value but never that it throws the right error, never any async rejection paths. It's like it only knows how to write the 'it works in the demo' test.

We used Copilot to bootstrap tests for a new module and hit 80% coverage on the first pass — looked great until code review where my lead pointed out every single test was a sunny-day scenario. Our coverage number was a lie.

clusters.title: VS Code Extension Crashes and Fails Silently
clusters.summary: Users report the VS Code extension frequently enters a broken state where suggestions stop appearing entirely, with no error message or status indicator to explain why — requiring users to reload the window or reinstall the extension to recover. The lack of visible diagnostic feedback makes it impossible to distinguish between a network issue, an authentication problem, or an extension bug.
verbatims: At least twice a week Copilot just stops suggesting anything. No error, no notification, the icon still shows as active. I've learned the fix is to reload VS Code but I shouldn't have to do that — I want to know what broke.

After the last extension update the inline completions disappeared for two days. I re-authenticated, checked my subscription, everything looked fine. Finally a window reload fixed it. Why is there zero feedback when it's in a broken state?

The Copilot status bar icon is basically decorative. It shows a checkmark whether it's working or completely dead. I've started pinging the Copilot Chat as a smoke test every morning because I can't trust the extension to tell me if it's actually connected.
